arguments.prompt: Point of view from the Mayor's office window, looking down between two giant limestone columns at a long timber rally stage under construction far out in the square below, thirty metres from the building, with empty wet granite paving between the balustrade and the stage. A heavy flat overcast, sheet-cake grey sky, no sun and no shadows; a light steady drizzle falls, fine rain visible against the dark stone, the granite paving wet with shallow puddles mirroring the grey sky; street lamps and windows glow warm and are doubled in the wet. The camera is locked off on a tripod and does not move at all: no pan, no tilt, no zoom, no drift, no handheld shake. Real-time speed, natural human movement, never slow motion. Six workmen in high-visibility vests move at a normal working pace around the platform, two carrying a decking board together to the open joists on the right, one kneeling to fix a board at the boundary; the two tall bare uprights stand still. Beyond the stage the square goes about its morning: parked cars do not move, the lumber truck and open box van stand still, a bus is stopped at the far corner, a few pedestrians walk slowly at a distance with their backs to us, a cyclist rolls by. Nobody walks across the empty paving below the balustrade. On the far street beyond the square and along the side kerbs a few cars move slowly and steadily with their headlights and tail-lights on, reflected in the wet road, at an unhurried city pace - no car ever enters the square or comes near the stage. Prestige political drama photographed on an Arri Alexa with anamorphic lenses: flat overcast daylight, slight 35mm film grain, colours desaturated about twelve percent, warm tungstens, deep browns and charcoals in the shadows, photographic realism.
